text:
One hundred years to the night after the franchise's first game, against these same Bruins, the Red Wings stuck with Daniil Tarasov in net and took the first lead. Boston took everything after that, 4-1, and snapped a three-game winless run.

Lucas Raymond's slap shot late in the first put Detroit ahead. The second period belonged to Boston, by 1.28 to 0.69 in expected goals (the quality of the chances). JJ Peterka tied it early on a 9% chance; Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub wrote that every time Peterka shoots, "you're reminded why he should shoot more." Pavel Zacha, whose name keeps turning up in trade talk, then scored on Boston's only power play, and that goal moved the Bruins' win chance from 51% to 72%. David Pastrnak made it 3-1 in the third with a snap shot, one of his six shots on goal, and Casey Mittelstadt added a late fourth.

Zacha, Pastrnak and Mittelstadt each had a goal and an assist and took the three stars. Behind them, Jeremy Swayman stopped 20 of 21, 1.1 goals better than expected, including Viktor Arvidsson's 30% look in the third. Boston deserved to win 60% of the time and blocked 23 shots, which is part of why Detroit had 65 attempts and only 21 on goal.

For Detroit, the problem was the old one. The Red Wings went 3-6 in their first nine games after Dylan Larkin left the team on Oct. 29 to wait for a trade, per the Detroit Free Press, and nights like this, with one goal on 2.06 expected, show what a lineup without its top center looks like against a structured team. Reports from the Free Press and Darren Dreger say the standoff is about Larkin's list and Detroit's price, and nothing in this game made it easier to wait.

Boston gets two points it needed, and a night where its stars looked like stars again.
headline: Bruins spoil Detroit's centennial night
